coverage_note: § 19 (pre-phenomenal temporality) and § 56 (the temporal structure of the kinaesthetic sequences), the two sections where temporality is thematic. The remaining 30 sections with term hits - among them §§ 20, 25, 26 and 62 - are not extracted.

units.claim: The immanent extension and divisibility of perception that survives the reduction is named pre-phenomenal or transcendental temporality and sharply distinguished from the phenomenal temporality attributed to objects.
units.quote: This immanent extension is what Husserl calls **pre-phenomenal** or **transcendental temporality**, and he sharply distinguishes it from **phenomenal temporality**, which is the time attributed to objects — the time of things as constituted through the apprehension.

units.claim: Two temporal forms are distinguished in every perception, one reell and one intentional, with the warning that the form of intuition is not the form of the intuited.
units.quote: Husserl warns against confusing them: the "form of intuition" (the immanent temporal form of the perceptual appearance) is not the same as the "form of the intuited" (the temporal form of the appearing thing).

units.claim: The temporal unity of perception is declared primary: phases are dependent moments of an already continuous whole rather than independent pieces later joined by synthesis.
units.quote: It is not that discrete perceptual phases first exist independently and are then joined by a subsequent synthesis. Rather, perception is always already a continuous, unbroken unity.

units.claim: The constitution of temporal position - what distinguishes now from just past, and the perpetual sinking of the Now - is posed as an immense difficulty the lectures defer.
units.quote: What accounts for the distinction between "now" and "just past"? What explains the perpetual self-generation of the Now and its perpetual sinking back into the past — the "eternal drama" as Husserl puts it — in which every past itself becomes a *further* past?

units.claim: Givenness is said to be carried out as a process in phenomenological temporality, the total phenomenon with its kinaesthetic and image components being temporally extended and having a changeable temporal form.
units.quote: But givenness is carried out as a **process in phenomenological temporality**: the total phenomenon, with its K-component and its i-component, is temporally extended.

units.claim: The temporal form of the kinaesthetic-image stream is held irrelevant for the appearing object: the same thing stands there whatever the speed or direction of exploration.
units.quote: Whether I explore the thing quickly or slowly, whether I pause longer at one phase or another, whether I reverse and retrace my steps — the same stationary thing continually stands there with unchanged content, extending the fullness of its content in a temporal form that is one and the same: a density homogeneous throughout.

units.claim: The irrelevance is qualified: temporality does enter the objectivation as the duration of the unchanged thing, which finds its presentational foothold in the phenomenological temporality of the appearance.
units.quote: In the present case, the temporality has the form of the **duration of the unchanged, stationary thing**. The thing endures; its duration is constituted in the temporal stream of perception.

units.claim: Spatial things are contrasted with temporal objects such as melodies, whose constitution depends essentially on the temporal form of their presentation.
units.quote: the spatial thing is constituted in an appearance-manifold that can be traversed in any direction and at any rate, unlike temporal objects (melodies) whose constitution depends essentially on the temporal form of their presentation

units.claim: An editorial note is reported to record that this passage was published within the time-consciousness lectures, marking the intersection of the spatial and temporal constitutive analyses.
units.quote: A significant editorial note records that this passage (through the end of §56) was published within the time-consciousness lectures (Husserliana X).
